changed.was: When fire destroyed its Bardstown distillery in 1996, Heaven Hill moved its distilling to the Bernheim Distillery in Louisville, bought in 1999.
changed.now: Fire destroyed Heaven Hill's Bardstown distillery in 1996; neighbouring distillers made its whiskey under contract until it bought the Bernheim Distillery in Louisville in 1999.
changed.why: the old line had distilling move to Bernheim in 1996; for nearly three years Brown-Forman and Jim Beam made Heaven Hill's whiskey

changed.was: In 1948, after the war years had cut distilling short, Continental dropped Square from the name and brought the whiskey back as a four year old bottled in bond.
changed.now: In 1948 Continental dropped Square from the name and remade the whiskey as a four year old bottled in bond.
changed.why: no source gives the war as the cause or a gap before 1948; the sources say the name and the recipe changed that year

changed.was: named, by most accounts, for the Philadelphia square of that name

changed.was: Clove, vanilla and anise first, then the pepper of rye over a gentle sweetness of grain, and a dry, spicy finish.

changed.was: trade accounts describe a low rye mash, close to the 51 per cent line.
